entities.label: EventWindow
entities.summary:
The Suez Crisis, a pivotal event in modern history, occurred in 1956 when Israel, the United Kingdom, and France invaded Egypt, sparking a global conflict.

The invasion, led by Israeli Prime Minister David Ben-Gurion and British Prime Minister Anthony Eden, aimed to regain control of the Suez Canal, a strategic waterway connecting the Mediterranean Sea to the Red Sea through Egypt.

The crisis escalated into a full-blown war, involving the United States, the Soviet Union, and other international forces. The war led to the withdrawal of British, French, and Israeli forces from the Sinai Peninsula and the Gaza Strip. The crisis marked a significant shift in global politics, with the United States emerging as a dominant world power.

The Suez Crisis had far-reaching consequences, including a significant increase in oil prices and a re-evaluation of the role of the United States in international affairs. The crisis also led to the rise of new global leaders, including Egyptian President Gamal Abdel Nasser and Soviet Premier Nikita Khrushchev.

As David Ben-Gurion noted, 'The Suez War was a turning point in the history of the Middle East.' The crisis also marked the beginning of the end of British and French colonial rule in the region.

The Suez Crisis will be remembered as a pivotal moment in modern history, marking a significant shift in global politics and the emergence of new global leaders.
